## TL;DR

Completed a focused QA pass of the Work board at desktop width and 375px using the task worktree's auth-less development server and headless Playwright. The board and mobile queue rendered without page errors or horizontal document overflow. Human and Held filters changed independently and retained their choices across a reload. Existing tests already cover the behaviors most relevant to this task, including status-filter counts, visibility persistence, sort persistence, collapse behavior, and drag/drop. I found no reproducible defect, so there was no code fix to add. The QA evidence and the safety limitation around live drag mutations are recorded in `docs/qa/2026-11-work-board-filters.md`.

## Work and rationale

I first read the task definition and the UI/preview conventions, then inspected WorkView and the repo store where the requested interactions are implemented. Human and Held visibility are separate localStorage preferences. WorkView composes their hidden task IDs before rendering board columns, and the status-filter count uses that same filtered list. The view selection and collapse state are also persisted. Since these paths already existed, I chose to verify the behavior in the running app and inspect the corresponding tests before considering a change.

The app was served on localhost from this task worktree in auth-less preview mode. I used Playwright's bundled WebKit in explicit headless mode. At 1440px, the Work route showed the board, sort selector, board/pipeline switch, and Human/Held controls. I clicked each visibility control, checked its `aria-pressed` state, reloaded, and confirmed that both off states were restored. The desktop document width equaled the viewport width.

At 375px, Work rendered its dedicated mobile queue. Search and the Show, Updated, priority, area, story, and assignment filters were present. The controls remain inside a horizontally scrolling filter panel; the overall document width still equaled 375px. No page errors were recorded during initial rendering. Screenshots were captured to temporary local files for visual inspection; they are not committed.

I read the existing visibility tests and found coverage for independent filters, restoration on a second click, persistence across component remount, and status-filter counts. Nearby suites cover sort preference persistence, collapse/arrival behavior, mobile overflow, and board column drop semantics. I did not add a duplicate test because this pass did not uncover an implementation defect and the existing suites exercise the relevant state transitions.

The QA notes are in `docs/qa/2026-11-work-board-filters.md`. They distinguish what I observed live from the behaviors verified by repository tests and record the drag-and-drop constraint explicitly.

## Approaches tried

I started with code inspection to map the UI controls to state and test coverage. I then launched the auth-less server and used Playwright in a desktop viewport, followed by a 375px viewport. I used semantic/test selectors for the Human and Held buttons, asserted their pressed states before and after clicking, and reloaded the page to check the stored preference. I measured `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` against `innerWidth` at both sizes and inspected the mobile queue content.

For drag-and-drop, I reviewed the existing browser/component tests and checked the populated UI rather than moving a card. A successful drop would write a real task status change to this worktree, which is outside the purpose of a QA pass and would leave repository data altered. This keeps the live session read-only while still recording the live layout evidence and the test coverage for drop behavior.

## Challenges and blockers

There was no application blocker. The available task index is large and contains held/human tasks, so changing a card status during the live run would have affected real worktree state. I therefore did not perform a live drop. The drop interaction is covered by `src/ui-app/tests/board-column-drop.test.ts`; a fully isolated live drag test would require a disposable fixture-backed server or another data-isolated environment.

The task's checklist mentioned a scratch worktree for serving. The current task worktree is the explicitly authorized working directory, and the auth-less `just serve-noauth` helper is documented to run from a worktree rather than a main checkout. I served this worktree directly, without reading or editing the main checkout. No persistent server-owned preview or headed browser was opened.

No source changes were justified by observed behavior. I did not run a check or claim one passed in this draft; the required scoped RepoOS check remains the final verification step for handoff.

## Key learnings

The desktop board and mobile queue are intentionally different compositions. At phone width the UI switches to the task queue, and its filter panel contains more controls than can fit inline; the panel scrolls horizontally while the page itself remains within the viewport. This is useful to preserve in future responsive changes: page-level overflow is the regression to avoid, not internal horizontal scrolling of the filter strip.

The Human and Held header controls are independent filters over the queue, and their choice survives a full page reload. The status-filter count follows those same filters, avoiding a mismatch between the visible cards and the chip count. Existing tests already provide stronger repeatable coverage of these details than a new near-duplicate test would.

Finally, live QA against a repository-backed server can mutate real task data. For board drag testing, repository tests or a disposable fixture server are safer than moving a real card in the engineer's worktree. The report separates those test results from the live viewport observations so a reviewer can see exactly what was exercised.
